home.srTitle: Tom in Africa — photographic series and fine art prints
home.projectP1: In November 2024, we left Paris in our Toyota Land Cruiser HDJ80 to cross Africa all the way to South Africa. Over nearly six months, we traveled through more than twenty countries, meeting local people, artists and associations, to tell the story — in pictures — of an authentic, deeply human Africa.
home.projectP2: Beyond the adventure, this trip was a search for encounters, discoveries and understanding, especially around access to clean water. Through our photographs, we share the landscapes, the faces and the stories that shaped this mother-son crossing and changed how we see the world.
home.contactBody: Write to us — we reply directly to the address you provide.

notreAventure.metaDescription: Six months, more than twenty countries, a mother and son crossing Africa in a Toyota Land Cruiser HDJ80.
notreAventure.title: Our Journey
notreAventure.subtitle: Paris — Cape Town, by Toyota Land Cruiser HDJ80, mother and son.
notreAventure.bornFromDreamEyebrow: An adventure born from a dream
notreAventure.lead: What if the most beautiful journey wasn’t a destination, but the encounters made along the way?
notreAventure.intro: For nearly six months, we drove across Africa, from Paris all the way to South Africa. More than twenty countries, thousands of kilometers, and countless stories. This book is the record of that adventure.
notreAventure.canyonPhotoAlt: Tom and Charlotte in front of their Toyota Land Cruiser, in a red sandstone canyon
notreAventure.whoP1: We are Tom and Charlotte, a son and his mother, driven by the same curiosity for the world and for human encounters. A photographer, filmmaker and adventurer at heart, Tom had dreamed for years of crossing Africa by road. Charlotte passed on to him her love of travel and of the African continent. Together, we decided to turn that dream into a life project.
notreAventure.riverPhotoAlt: The Toyota Land Cruiser crossing a river in Nigeria
notreAventure.prep1: With no mechanical training, no camping experience, and nothing but the will to leave, we prepared our Toyota Land Cruiser HDJ80 and hit the road in November 2024. Our goal was never to set a record or achieve some feat. We wanted to take our time — time to get lost, to learn, to listen, and to understand.
notreAventure.projectP1: This crossing quickly became far more than a trip. Mile after mile, we sought out artists who use their creativity to help their societies move forward.
notreAventure.projectP2: From Sanae Arraqas in Morocco to Amy Sow in Mauritania, by way of Patrick Tagoe-Turkson in Ghana, each of them opened the doors of their world to us and shared their vision of it.
notreAventure.artistSanaePortraitAlt: Sanae Arraqas, a painter we met in Morocco
notreAventure.artistAmyPortraitAlt: Amy Sow, an artist we met in Mauritania
notreAventure.artistPatrickPortraitAlt: Patrick Tagoe-Turkson, an artist we met in Ghana
notreAventure.artistMosaicWorkAlt: A painted mosaic artwork, in Ghana
notreAventure.associationsP1: We also met associations working every day to improve life in their communities. On Gorée Island, Fallou Dolly and Cheikh Bamba reminded us that commitment and solidarity can change lives. In Ghana, Surf Ghana uses sport as a powerful tool for inclusion and empowerment.
notreAventure.waterP1: Another subject naturally kept coming up along the journey: access to clean water. In several villages, we tried to understand what life was like when every liter of water demanded hours of effort. These conversations became one of the throughlines of this adventure.
notreAventure.villageChiefPhotoAlt: Meeting a village chief and his community, under the palm trees
notreAventure.unexpectedP1: Of course, there were also the unexpected moments: endless tracks, police checks, broken-down ferries, nights spent in the middle of nowhere, mechanical problems, and times when everything seemed to fall apart. And yet, it’s often in those moments that we met the most extraordinary people.
notreAventure.cattlePhotoAlt: A herd crosses a village road in Cameroon, seen from the drone
notreAventure.welcomeP1: Through this book, we don’t just want to show you the landscapes of an exceptional continent. We want to take you along to share the daily life of the people who welcomed us, the stories they entrusted to us, and the emotions that turned this crossing into a deeply human adventure.
notreAventure.bookP1: A photography book will tell the story of these six months on the road, coming soon.
notreAventure.exhibitionP1: An exhibition will soon take place in Paris, built around the photographs from this crossing.

aPropos.metaDescription: Photographic approach, working method in the field, and how the prints are made.
aPropos.title:
Photographing what remains
when everything else is stripped away.
aPropos.bioPlaceholder: [TO COMPLETE: your bio — who you are, how long you’ve been photographing, what brought you to Africa.]
aPropos.approachP1: I work in series, over long stays, and I return to the same place several times. An image that holds up almost always requires having failed in that same spot before — and gone back knowing what to expect.
aPropos.approachP2: None of these photographs is a stolen shot. Animals are approached under simple rules: never close the distance, position yourself along their path, and accept coming back without an image. The people photographed know they are being photographed and have given their consent.
